haiku-low.q1: Its document is deleted from the index, written with version = commit_lsn, since non-active rows are deleted.
haiku-low.q2: The store returns a 409 version conflict for that document. It is counted as stale, not as an error.
haiku-low.q3: It retries that document with backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, capped at 60 s). The partition waits and never skips ahead.
haiku-low.q4: It is produced to catalog.products.dlq with the error text and source offset. An alert is raised and processing continues.
haiku-low.q5: At 20 GB ops are alerted. At 50 GB ops drop the slot, changes since then are lost, the index is marked stale, and a rebuild is required.
haiku-low.q6: After cutover: one atomic alias request moves products and products_write to products_v4. First the gate must pass: lag under 5 s and count within 0.5%, with live paused and replay caught up.
haiku-low.q7: Live progress is Kafka consumer offsets, committed after each batch is fully resolved. Rebuild state (S, replay start, last_id) is in the indexer's own Postgres, saved after each batch.
haiku-low.q8: The batch is read again from Kafka. Versions make the replay safe, so the writes are not harmful.
haiku-low.q9: Group indexer-rebuild replays each partition from the replay start and applies the live rules with version = commit_lsn into products_v4, alongside the bulk copy.
haiku-low.q10: Bulk-copied documents carry version = S, the snapshot LSN from pg_current_wal_lsn().
haiku-low.q11: For 48 hours the live consumer dual-writes to v3 and v4, so v3 stays current. Rollback is one atomic alias move back to v3. Deleting v3 after 48 hours with no rollback ends it.
haiku-low.q12: Search keeps using v3, since v4 has no alias until cutover. A copy failure resumes from last_id on a new snapshot. A failed gate loops back to replay or reconcile.

sonnet.q1: The document is deleted from the index (delete with version = commit_lsn), since only active rows may appear in search.
sonnet.q2: The store returns a 409 version conflict and does not apply the older write. It is counted as stale, not an error. This relies on the store keeping a version marker for deletes (to be verified).
sonnet.q3: It retries that document after 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, capped at 60 s. The partition waits and never skips ahead, and offsets are not committed until the batch is resolved.
sonnet.q4: On a 400 invalid response, the document is produced to catalog.products.dlq with the error text and source offset. An alert is raised and processing continues. Offsets commit once the DLQ produce is acknowledged.
sonnet.q5: At 20 GB of retained WAL ops are alerted. At 50 GB ops drop the slot to protect the primary. Changes since the drop are lost and the index is marked stale. A full rebuild is the only way back.
sonnet.q6: One atomic alias request points both products and products_write to products_v4. Before that, the gate must pass: rebuild lag under 5 s on every partition and products_v4 count within 0.5% of active rows. The live group must be paused, and the rebuild group's offsets must be at or past the live group's offsets on every partition.
sonnet.q7: Live indexer progress is stored as consumer group offsets in Kafka (group indexer-live). Offsets are committed only after every document in the batch is resolved (applied, stale, or DLQ produce acknowledged). Rebuild progress (job state, S, replay start, last_id) is in a progress store, in the indexer's own Postgres. last_id is saved after each batch.
sonnet.q8: The uncommitted batch is read again from Kafka and rewritten. Versions make the replay safe, because already-applied documents get a 409 and are counted as stale.
sonnet.q9: The indexer-rebuild group replays the topic from the replay start (snapshot start minus 10 minutes) alongside the copy. It writes into products_v4 with version = commit_lsn. Changes at or before S are already in the snapshot, and older events are refused as stale. Changes after S have commit_lsn > S and are applied.
sonnet.q10: Version = S, the pg_current_wal_lsn() read at the start of the snapshot transaction. After a crash and resume, a new snapshot S2 is opened and that version is used for later batches.
sonnet.q11: products_v3 stays open. For 48 hours the live consumer writes to both v4 and v3 and commits offsets only when both acknowledge. If a v3 write fails, the commit waits and an alert is raised. Rollback is one atomic alias request back to v3, which is already current. After 48 hours with no rollback, writes to v3 stop and it is deleted.
sonnet.q12: Search is unaffected. products_v4 has no alias until cutover, so the search API never sees it and keeps using products_v3. The live sync keeps running. On a crash or lost connection the copy resumes from the saved last_id with a new snapshot S2. The replay start stays fixed. Resuming after a mid-job failure that cannot be recovered is NOT STATED.
